newsitem.title: POLAND: No heavy rain expected in Poland in coming days.
newsitem.headline: No heavy rain expected in Poland in coming days.

text.p: Occasional showers may fall on flood-hit southern and western parts of Poland in the coming two days, but no prolonged or heavy rain, an official of the country's Meteorology and Water Management Institute said.
"In the coming two days we are expecting occasional showers over the (flood-affected) area and there is also a possibilty of thunderstorms," the official told Reuters on Wednesday.
"But there will be no heavy, continual rains, only five to 10 millimetres in 24 hours," he added.
Heavy rains in early July provoked more than two weeks of disastrous flooding, affecting 5,000 sq km and killing at least 55 people.

On Tuesday flood crisis committee officials said the total death toll from the region's worst flood disaster in centuries was 60, but police later said five of these deaths were unrelated to the floods.
A new bout of rain over the weekend plunged several communities, which were just emerging from the deluge or had so far escaped damage, back under the flood waters.

This latest rain caused another swell of high water to sweep north along the Odra river, but it was about 1.5 metres lower than the one which earlier devastated Wroclaw and Opole, flood control officials said.
Both cities have been bracing for the new wave, which though lower is still dangerous for some areas as flood defences have been weakened by the earlier onslaught.
